correctness.rationale: The exact Gram eigenprojector formula (1) and independent beta-prime radial/Beta angular laws (2) reconstruct the risk. At s=3 the 2x2 Wishart determinant exponent vanishes; integrating ordered eigenvalues gives angle density proportional to a(theta)^(-2), whose two rational angular integrals yield epsilon^2/(1+epsilon^2). For s=2 the radial density is (1+r)^(-2), and the large-x kernel is Et^2/x+O(x^-2)=1/(2x)+O(x^-2), hence epsilon^2 log(1/epsilon)+O(epsilon^2). For fixed s>2 the region r<2epsilon^2 is O(epsilon^s)=o(epsilon^2), and dominated convergence on its complement yields Et^2 E(1/r)=1/(s-2). Definitions and ranges (m>=s>=2, 0<epsilon<1, independent real Gaussian sketch) and exact/nonasymptotic vs asymptotic conclusions are explicit. The embedded verifier passed 1,500 Gram-eigenvector identities, 18 three-row integration identities, and 10 radial-asymptotic numerical sanity checks; finite checks are not substituted for proofs.

value.rationale: The precise mean squared angular error is the natural null-space/smallest-singular-vector recovery observable in sketched SVD (Nakatsukasa–Park 2022). The minimal sketch s=2 has a provably unavoidable logarithmic amplification from near-singular Gaussian projections, and one extra row removes it; s=3 has an exact finite-condition-number benchmark for testing algorithms and perturbation analyses. These are substantive endpoint and oversampling thresholds rather than a routine inequality. Value pertains to a meaningful two-singular-mode test model, not to general spectra or production floating-point behavior.
